claim: People misremembering their 2024 vote, combined with weighting polls to past vote, may be adding a bit under one point to Republicans in generic-ballot polls.
Called 2025 off-year polling Republican-favored and pointed to late effects of the government shutdown as the likeliest reason.
magnitude: 5 to 10 points in NJ and VA

claim: Describes recalled-vote weighting as one of the tricks making 2026 polls look worse for Republicans than they are.
Suggested Midwest Republicans may again beat their polls, as they did in 2018 and 2024.
evidence: TV analysis, as reported by TheBlaze

claim: Weighting by party affiliation made its 2020 and 2024 post-election polls about 2 to 3 points more accurate on the margin; Republicans have become slightly less likely to take part in polls.
points_to: Unweighted polls lean Democratic; weighting corrects

claim: No single method guaranteed accuracy in 2024. Republican-affiliated pollsters were slightly more accurate, which the task force says may reflect releasing friendlier numbers in a year when the average leaned Democratic.
points_to: Accuracy rankings can reward a lean

claim: Its likely-voter adjustment moves the 2026 generic-ballot average half a point toward Democrats.
Prefers a soft likely-voter screen over aggressive filtering of respondents through complex turnout models.
evidence: Rough transcript of his stream remarks, relayed via ChatGPT; not independently verified
